title: Canonical additive-functor map of strict Roos complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with countable products [def-weil-category-product], let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive, and let $C:\mathbf N^{op}\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(\mathcal A,\mathbf Z)$ be a strict tower [def-weil-inverse-system]. Use the strict Roos construction [def-sf-strict-roos-functor]. Define $b_C=1-s_C$ [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism] and the map $\kappa_{F,C}:F(\operatorname{Roos}(C))\to\operatorname{Roos}(F C)$ as the unique chain map with both prescribed product coordinates: its unshifted coordinate followed by the $n$th projection is $F(\operatorname{fst}\,;\operatorname{pr}_n)$; in degree $i$, its shifted coordinate followed by the $n$th degree $i-1$ projection is $F(\operatorname{snd}^i\,;\operatorname{pr}_n^{i-1})$. Here $F$ is applied termwise to complexes. Thus both coordinates use the canonical product comparison, without an arbitrary completion of a triangle. No exactness or product-preservation assumption is part of this definition.
